$comment: The words of every woven event. The rules for when each can happen are in src/content/happenings.ts;
everything a player reads is here, so a sentence can be rewritten without touching code.
Each template names the `slots` it may use, and a slot is written {like_this}. The code fills them
from what is on the tile; test/happenings.test.ts refuses a slot a template did not declare, a
template the code has and this file does not (or the other way round), and a choice nobody uses.
A value is a string, or a record of variants when one template says different things in
different circumstances: the three kinds of weather, or whether you know a stranger's name yet.
Diary voice: second person, past the moment, British spelling. Nobody fails; every choice is a
real one with its own line. Strangers are 'they'. English only, with Jambhudweepan nouns, by

tracks.title: Tracks across the path
tracks.prose: Pressed into the ground across your way, and fresh: the tracks of {a_animal}. They cross from one side to the other and are lost in {ground} a few strides on.

follow.label: Follow them a little way
follow.line: You follow the {animal}'s tracks until the ground stops holding them. You never see it. You know now where it crosses, which is most of what anybody who tracks for a living knows.

leave.label: Step round them
leave.line: You step round the tracks rather than over them, and leave them for whoever comes by next.

dropped.title: Something on the road
dropped.prose: Somebody has dropped a little {material} at the side of the road. Fallen from a load, by the look of it, and not worth going back for.

take.label: Pick it up
take.line: You pick up the {material}. Whoever dropped it was carrying more than they could keep hold of.

leave.label: Leave it where it fell
leave.line: You leave the {material} where it fell, in case whoever dropped it comes back along the road.

company.title: Company on the road
company.prose: A {role}, falls in beside you for a stretch. Dressed in {dye} gone pale with the road's dust, and in no hurry to be anywhere but walking.

line.named: You walk together as far as the next turning. Their name is {name}, and that is most of what they say; the miles go easier for it.
line.unnamed: You walk together as far as the next turning. Neither of you says much, and the miles go easier for it.

line.named: They point you on toward {elsewhere}, and say it is further than it looks. It usually is. They give their name as {name} before they turn off.
line.unnamed: They point you on toward {elsewhere}, and say it is further than it looks. It usually is.

prose.named: {name}, the {trade} from the other day, is on the road ahead, still in {dye}, and lifts a hand when they see it is you.
prose.unnamed: The {trade} from the other day is on the road ahead, still in {dye}, and lifts a hand when they see it is you.

catch-up.label: Catch them up
catch-up.line: You fall in together as if you had arranged it. They remember which way you were going, which is more than most people do.

wave.label: Lift a hand back
wave.line: You lift a hand back and let the road carry them on ahead. It is good to be known somewhere.

prose.rain: Rain comes across {ground} in a grey sheet, and then it is on you.
prose.mist: The mist comes down so quickly that {ground} behind you is gone before you have turned to look.
prose.storm: The sky goes the colour of a bruise, and the first of the wind flattens {ground} ahead of you.

wait.label: Wait it out under the {plant}
wait.line: You wait under the {plant} until the worst has passed. It is not a roof, but it is a good deal better than none.

stand.label: Stand and let it pass
stand.line: You turn your back to it and wait where you are. It passes, as it always does, and {ground} comes back washed.

line.rain: You walk on through it, soaked within a hundred steps, after which there is nothing more it can do to you.
line.mist: You walk on slowly, counting steps, and the ground comes back one stride at a time.
line.storm: You walk on with your head down, and the storm goes over you rather than through you.

night-sounds.title: Something beyond the lamp
night-sounds.prose: Late, with the lamp turned low, something moves at the edge of its light. By the sound of it, {a_animal}: out at the hour it likes best, and not much interested in you.

listen.label: Keep still and listen
listen.line: You keep still and listen until it has gone about its business. You could not have drawn it, but you would know that sound again.

lamp.label: Turn up the lamp
lamp.line: You turn up the lamp. For a moment there are two eyes at the edge of the light, and then there are none.

dream.title: A dream
dream.prose: You dream of {ground} before anybody had walked there: the same ground, the same light, and nobody at all to write it down.

write.label: Write it down before it goes
write.line: You write it down by feel in the dark. In the morning half of it will not read, and the other half is better than you remembered.

let.label: Let it go
let.line: You let it go. By first light you remember only that it was quiet.

knock.title: Somebody after dark
knock.prose: After dark there is a voice at the edge of your shelter: a {role}, caught out by the night and asking whether there is room for one more.

line.named: They give their name as {name}, sleep sitting up against their load, and are gone before you wake. The night was warmer for two.
line.unnamed: They sleep sitting up against their load and are gone before you wake. The night was warmer for two.

line.named: You point them on toward {elsewhere}. They thank you, say their name is {name} in case you meet again, and go.
line.unnamed: You point them on toward {elsewhere}. They thank you and go, and the night is quiet again.

cairn.title: Stones at the edge
cairn.prose: At the edge of {place} somebody once began a little pile of stones, and everybody who has arrived since has added one.

add.label: Add a stone
add.line: You add a stone to the pile. It is not a large one, but it is yours, and it will be here after you have gone.

count.label: Count them
count.line: You count {count} before you lose your place, which is a great many arrivals for somewhere this quiet.

cookfire.title: A fire already lit
cookfire.prose: There is smoke going up at {place}, and the smell of something in a pot. Whoever is tending it waves you over before you have properly arrived.

eat.label: Accept a bowl
eat.line: You eat sitting on your heels by the fire. Nobody asks where you have come from until the bowl is empty, which is good manners anywhere.

wave.label: Wave back and go on
wave.line: You wave back and go on into {place}. The smell follows you further than the smoke does.

watched.title: Being watched
watched.prose: You look up from the work to find {a_animal} watching you from close by, with the air of something that has seen this done before and thinks you are doing it wrong.

carry-on.label: Carry on regardless
carry-on.line: You carry on. When you look up again it has gone, satisfied or disappointed; there is no telling which.

watch.label: Stop and watch it back
watch.line: You stop and watch it back. Neither of you moves for a long moment, and then it decides you are not interesting and goes.

underneath.title: Something underneath
underneath.prose: Under what you were taking, the ground gives up something else: a little {material}, turned up by the work.

keep.label: Keep it
keep.line: You keep the {material}. The ground is generous to anybody who bothers to look at it.

back.label: Put it back
back.line: You put it back where it was and press the earth down over it.
